description: FIRST MULTI-BODY GOLDEN (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-0 — the plumbing de-risker, no user-visible boolean): a part that ENDS WITH TWO disjoint bodies. Four features: (1) a 20x20 mm square on the XY origin datum at x,y in [0,20]; (2) extrude add 20 mm up -> body A, a 20x20x20 cube (merge absent -> reads True, the historical single-body behaviour: creates the first body); (3) a second 20x20 mm square on the SAME XY datum but at x in [30,50] (a 10 mm gap from body A); (4) extrude add 20 mm up with merge=FALSE -> body B, a SECOND independent 20x20x20 cube, NOT fused into A. The part now holds bodies={A, B} with B active. Locks the MB-0 pipeline end to end: (a) merge=False starts a new active body keyed by its base feature id (EvaluationState.bodies/active_body_id); (b) the analytic compound roll-up composes the part mass properties over the body set (Sigma volume, volume-weighted centroid, unioned AABB, summed faces/edges/shells -- NO re-mesh, NO boolean, the assembly _combine_properties pattern); (c) tessellation over a build123d Compound of both bodies (glb_stats sums the two meshes); and -- via the parametrized round-trip gate -- STEP multi-solid export (valid AP214) + re-import. Bodies are TREE-ORDERED (A before B by base order_index) and the compound is assembled in that fixed order, so the in-process and fresh-interpreter determinism gates require byte-identical GLB + identical metadata across an interpreter restart.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Body A: an axis-aligned 20x20 square, corners (0,0)-(20,20) mm on the XY datum (normal +Z at world z=0); extrude add 20 mm up -> cube A spanning x,y in [0,20], z in [0,20]. Body B: a 20x20 square at corners (30,0)-(50,20) mm on the same XY datum; extrude add 20 mm up with merge=false -> cube B spanning x in [30,50], y in [0,20], z in [0,20]. The 10 mm gap in x (A ends at x=20, B starts at x=30) makes the bodies DISJOINT -- they share no face, edge, or vertex.

volume = A + B = 20*20*20 + 20*20*20 = 8000 + 8000 = 16000 mm^3 exactly. The bodies are disjoint, so the sum is exact with no overlap subtraction. Measured deviation vs analytic: ~4e-12 mm^3 (a couple of ulp at the 1.6e4 scale, from the two independent GProp integrations summed in float64).
surface_area = 2 cubes * 6 faces * (20*20 = 400) = 2 * 2400 = 4800 mm^2. Every face of both cubes is external (nothing is fused), so all 12 faces contribute. Measured deviation: ~1e-12 mm^2.

centroid = (25, 10, 10) mm: cube A (V=8000, centroid (10,10,10)) and cube B (V=8000, centroid (40,10,10)) give x = (8000*10 + 8000*40)/16000 = 400000/16000 = 25.0; y = 10 and z = 10 by symmetry (both cubes share y in [0,20], z in [0,20]). Volume-weighted, computed analytically over the body set (combine_properties), never re-meshed. Measured deviation: x exactly 25.0, z exactly 10.0, y within 2e-15 of 10.0 (GProp ulp).

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[50,20,20]: the union of A's AABB [0,0,0]..[20,20,20] and B's AABB [30,0,0]..[50,20,20]. Extrusion of a planar face is an exact prism and the union of two axis-aligned boxes is exact, so all six bounds are EXACT (measured deviation 0.0).

topology (summed over the body set, NOT a boolean union): each cube has 6 faces, 12 edges, 1 closed shell -> 12 faces, 24 edges, 2 SHELLS. shells=2 is the load-bearing multi-body assertion: the part is genuinely two lumps, so the shell count is 2, not 1. Per-cube Euler-Poincare cross-check: V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 2 = 2*(1-0), a valid closed manifold solid; the part is two such shells.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, faceted per-face normals, no vertex sharing across faces -- the box-golden convention): each cube face is a planar quad -> 4 vertices / 2 triangles; 6 faces per cube = 24 vertices / 12 triangles; two cubes = 48 vertices / 24 triangles. glb_stats sums over the compound's two meshes.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). This is TWO disjoint planar B-reps (Solid.extrude prisms) whose properties are composed ANALYTICALLY (combine_properties: Sigma volume, volume-weighted centroid, unioned AABB) -- no boolean, no AABB padding. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-18, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume ~4e-12 mm^3, surface_area ~1e-12 mm^2, bounding_box exactly 0.0 on all six bounds, centroid x/z exact and y <= 2e-15 mm. Documented ceiling 1e-9 is ~250x the observed worst case (~4e-12, volume -- the sum of two independent GProp integrations), headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). The solver contributes zero error by construction (both squares are shape-pinned, under-constrained only in whole-sketch position -> planegcs returns the drawn positions bitwise; solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
